title: KV staging-ring + stride-prefetch hybrid for blocked/paged GPU KV cache
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: We see frequent micro-OOMs and latency spikes when long-context workloads with strided attention cause repetitive non-sequential KV touches. Existing paged/blocked allocator tends to either overfetch contiguous pages (wasting GPU memory) or underfetch (causing synchronous host->GPU transfers and tail latency).

Goal: Prototype and validate a hybrid runtime component — a KV staging-ring plus stride-prefetch heuristics — to reduce synchronous page faults and smooth latency under continuous batching. The staging-ring is a small host/GPU resident ring buffer for recently-evicted page fragments that can be rehydrated into GPU memory cheaply. Stride-prefetch observes token access patterns across in-flight batches and issues targeted async prefetches of pages whose access stride indicates near-term reuse.

Design summary:
- Staging ring: fixed-size circular host staging buffer (configurable per pool) that stores compressed page fragments evicted from GPU. When a page is re-requested, ring lookup can serve a rehydrate path that is ~3-6x faster than pulling from remote object store or full host swap. Evictions to ring are soft; when ring occupancy is high, oldest fragments are flushed to host swap.
- Stride-prefetch: lightweight stride sampler attached to per-worker batch queue. For each KV handle, maintain recent access offsets (last N tokens) and compute a stride score. If score > threshold and target page not resident, enqueue an async prefetch with priority proportional to predicted time-to-use and batch latency budget.
- Integration with continuous batching: prefetch scheduler is batch-aware: it groups prefetchs with pending GPU kernels to leverage existing DMA bursts and minimize PCIe setup cost. Prefetches are throttled based on current batch SLO headroom and residency budgets to avoid increasing tail latency for other requests.
- Fallbacks: When prefetch misses or staging-ring lookup fails, fall back to existing host->GPU swap protocol. For high thermal or memory pressure, degrade to conservative prefetching (only while batch queue depth < X).

Trade-offs considered:
- Memory vs latency: Staging ring uses host RAM to reduce GPU thrash; large rings reduce rehydration misses but increase host memory and GC pressure.
- Complexity: Stride detection adds per-handle metadata and CPU cycles; we keep sampler window small (N=8) and amortize capture across batches.
- Correctness: Must handle multi-tenant evictions and page aliasing across model shards. Staging ring entries tagged with model-version + page-id + slot-epoch.

Prototype metrics (early local experiments):
- Setup: 1xA100 80GB, 6 concurrent chat sessions (avg seq len 1024), continuous batching enabled (batch size ~24 steady).
- Baseline: 95th latency = 320ms, host->GPU sync faults per minute = 78.
- With staging-ring (64MB) + stride-prefetch (threshold tuned): 95th latency = 210ms, sync faults per minute = 18. Token throughput unchanged.
- Observed regression case: bursty random-access synthetic workload increased background prefetch traffic and raised 50th percentile by ~12ms. Addressed by adding batch headroom-aware throttling.

Open design decisions and next steps:
1) Staging ring format: currently prototype uses LZ4-compressed 4KB fragments. Need investigation of GPU decompress cost vs PCIe transfer time; potential to implement hardware-accelerated decompression on future HW.
2) Prefetch scoring: simple linear regression vs exponential moving average — we currently use EMA with alpha=0.35; evaluate learned predictor later.
3) Multi-GPU shard coordination: whether to replicate staging-ring metadata across workers or maintain a coordinator service. Prototype keeps metadata per-host and uses soft invalidation. Consider global coordinator if cross-shard reuse is dominant.

Testing / rollout plan:
- Short-term (this cycle): finalize allocator hooks, land prototype in experimental runtime flag, add microbench harness (synthetic stride patterns + chat traces), collect telemetry (prefetch hit rate, ring rehydrate latency, extra PCIe bytes), and run canary on internal staging.
- Mid-term: enable flag for 5% of hosted traffic for models with >8k context and >10% page churn, monitor SLOs, regressions, and cost delta.
- Long-term: expose tuning knobs in console (ring_size, prefetch_threshold, sampler_window), add automated tuning suggestions in Optimize.

comments: 2025-01-12 — Diego: initial spike prototype landed on branch eng/kv-staging. Observed unstable rehydrate path when running >64 concurrent sessions; probably race in slot epoch handling.
2025-01-15 — Aisha: added slot-epoch tagging and soft invalidation to avoid stale rehydrates. Microbench updated. Please review PR for thread-safety comments.
2025-01-20 — Maria (runtime perf): stride sampler cost looks fine, but we need to limit sampler updates to batch commit path to reduce cacheline contention on hot handles.
2025-01-24 — QA: synthetic regression workload showed prefetch amplification during long random runs. Diego added batch-headroom throttling and a simple per-worker rate limiter.
2025-01-28 — Diego: replaced LZ4 config with adaptive compress-level=1 during high-throughput runs (lower CPU cost); planning a GPU-decompress evaluation for next week.
2025-02-01 — PM review: target mid-Feb canary approved by product; ensure telemetry events include prefetch_reason, predicted_ttu_ms, and ring_rehydrate_latency_ms.
